title: Why must a rigid job receive its whole gang?
scope: Original pool: GPU 0–7. Both J1 and J2 require all eight GPUs. The two scheduling policies are alternative runs.

steps.label: Empty pool
steps.description: Both jobs need the complete pool; no job can compute with a partial allocation.

steps.label: Hold half and wait
steps.description: Partial scheduling gives J1 GPUs 0–3 and J2 GPUs 4–7. Each waits for resources held by the other; neither can compute.
cards: Alternative gang run has not started

steps.label: Atomic grant to J1
steps.description: In the alternative gang run J1 receives all eight at once. J2 waits while holding zero; there is no circular hold.

steps.label: Release, then grant J2
steps.description: J1 finishes and releases the complete pool before J2 acquires it. Atomic admission prevents this allocation deadlock, though queueing remains.

guard: No claimed wall time, utilization gain, fairness, or general deadlock freedom.
